newsitem.title: CANADA: Railways shut Red River lines as grain rushed out.
newsitem.headline: Railways shut Red River lines as grain rushed out.

text.p: Canadian railways shut their Red River Valley lines on Wednesday as grain handlers scrambled to rush grain out of a flood zone projected to cover 800 square miles (2,072 square km), officials said.
"The Letellier line to the U.S. was shut this morning," Canadian National Railway Co spokesman, Jim Feeny said.
CP Rail System closed its Emerson line which links with its SOO Line in the United States at 1600 EDT/2000 GMT Tuesday, CP spokesman Steve Morris said.
Floods in 1950 and 1979 left 400 square miles (1,036 square km) of land between the U.S. border and Winnipeg under water.
This year's flood may well cover double that area and take weeks to drain, Manitoba Natural Resources flood liaison engineer Larry Whitney said.
"We got most grain out in the earlier projected area (400 square miles) but with this expanded level it throws the earlier numbers out," Manitoba Pool Elevators president Charlie Swanson said.
MPE facilities handled more than 50 percent of Manitoba grain and oilseed capacity in the last crop year.
"Some farmers thought they were safe and now they found out that they're not, so there's people scrambling to get grain out. We've taken in quite a lot and we're moving it wherever we can."
Grain industry sources said most threatened grains and oilseeds would likely be trucked out before head waters flood the outlying areas of the Red River Valley.
